title: Controller → ActionResult → Status Codes
blurb: The request reached the controller. Now match each ActionResult helper to the HTTP status code it actually returns — including the pairs everyone confuses.

docs.label: Microsoft Learn — Controller action return types

levels.title: L1 · The everyday four
levels.prompt: Connect each ActionResult helper to the status code it returns.

failStates.title: Created is 201, not 200
failStates.explain: CreatedAtAction() returns 201 and sets a Location header pointing at the new resource. 200 is for a plain successful read/update with no 'something new was created' semantics.

failStates.title: Ok() is 200, not 201
failStates.explain: Ok() is a 200 — success with a body. 201 specifically signals a resource was created and comes from Created()/CreatedAtAction().

levels.title: L2 · The confusing pairs
levels.prompt: These are the ones people mix up. Match each helper to its code.

failStates.title: 403 vs 401
failStates.explain: Forbid() is 403: 'I know who you are, and you're not allowed.' 401 is 'I don't know who you are — authenticate first.' Authentication problem → 401; permission problem → 403.

failStates.title: 401 vs 403
failStates.explain: Unauthorized() is 401 — credentials are missing or invalid. 403 (Forbid) is for an authenticated user who simply isn't permitted.

failStates.title: 422 vs 400
failStates.explain: 400 means the request was malformed (couldn't even be parsed). 422 means it parsed fine but failed validation rules — well-formed, but semantically invalid.
